agree.reason: The safety record and adult-training experience make a fair case for a phone screen, but a skeptical HR manager may still see a teacher who hasn't worked in GMP and offers no concrete plan for closing that gap.

honest.reason: Every claim matches the brief, the seven years since 2019 is correct for 2026, and the letter leaves out the unsupported promise to halve training time instead of asserting it.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated as given and never developed: roughly 980 student-years without a serious injury, about 24 hours of adult training a year, and a 17-point pass-rate gain (about 41% relative) are all left uncalculated.

right_comparison.reason: The letter compares new teachers with plant new hires, but it never says what the plant's current training or onboarding looks like, so there is no baseline to improve on, and the AP trend has no baseline either.

qualification.reason: The hedge "I would need to learn the record-keeping rules and the software" gives no timeline, target or way for the reader to check progress, such as becoming proficient in the LMS within a stated number of weeks.

objections.reason: It addresses the lack of regulated-industry, GMP-records and LMS experience head-on and links it to procedural discipline, though "the habit I already have" asserts more than it shows.

fit.reason: It is a conventional cover letter that fits on one page, and dropping the halve-training-time claim was a reasonable judgment call even though the user asked for it.
